requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: The `with` statement IS used to associate attributes to TTCN-3 language elements and to sets of language elements.
requirements.original: The with statement is used to associate attributes to TTCN-3 language elements (and sets thereof).

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: The `with` statement has the syntax `with "{" { ( encode | variant | display | extension | optional ) [ override | @local ] [ "(" DefinitionRef | FieldReference | AllRef ")" ] [ ( FreeText | ( "{" FreeText { "," FreeText } "}" ) ) "." ] FreeText [ ";" ] } "}"`.
requirements.original:
with "{" 
   { ( encode | variant | display | extension | optional )
    [ override | @local ]
    ["(" DefinitionRef | FieldReference | AllRef ")"] 
    [ ( FreeText | ("{" FreeText { "," FreeText } "}") ) "." ] FreeText [";"] }
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.canonical: There ARE five kinds of attributes that can be associated with a language element: display, encode, variant, extension and optional.
requirements.original: There are five kinds of attributes that can be associated to language elements:

requirements.subject: ent:display-attribute
requirements.canonical: The `display` attribute IS allowing the specification of display attributes related to specific presentation formats.
requirements.original: a) display: allows the specification of display attributes related to specific presentation formats;

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: The `encode` attribute IS allowing references to specific encoding rules.
requirements.original: b) encode: allows references to specific encoding rules;

requirements.subject: ent:variant-attribute
requirements.canonical: The `variant` attribute IS allowing references to specific encoding variants.
requirements.original: c) variant: allows references to specific encoding variants;

requirements.subject: ent:extension-attribute
requirements.canonical: The `extension` attribute IS allowing the specification of user-defined attributes.
requirements.original: d) extension: allows the specification of user-defined attributes;

requirements.subject: ent:optional-attribute
requirements.canonical: The `optional` attribute IS allowing the implicit setting of optional fields of records and sets to `omit`.
requirements.original: e) optional: allows the implicit setting of optional fields in records and sets to omit.

requirements.subject: ent:free-text
requirements.canonical: The argument of an attribute in a `with` statement (the actual attribute) IS a free text string.
requirements.original: The syntax for the argument of the with statement (i.e. the actual attributes) is defined as a free text string.

requirements.subject: ent:definition-ref
requirements.canonical: A DefinitionRef or FieldReference in a `with` statement IS identifying a definition or field, respectively, within the module, group or definition to which the `with` statement is associated.
requirements.original: _DefinitionRef and FieldReference identify a definition or field respectively which is within the module, group or_ definition to which the with statement is associated.

requirements.subject: ent:all-ref
requirements.canonical: An AllRef MAY be used to apply attributes to multiple language elements defined within the scope to which the `with` statement is associated.
requirements.original: _AllRef can be used to apply attributes to multiple language elements defined within the scope to which the with_ statement is associated.

requirements.subject: ent:all-ref
requirements.canonical: An AllRef IS selecting all language elements, or all language elements of a certain kind, defined in a given scope.
requirements.original: AllRef provides a flexible mechanism to select all language elements or all language elements of a certain kind defined in a given scope.

requirements.subject: ent:except-clause
requirements.canonical: An individual language element that is not affected by an attribute MAY be excluded from a set of language elements selected by an AllRef by means of the except clause.
requirements.original: Individual language elements that are not affected by an attribute can be excluded from a set of selected language elements in the except clause.

requirements.subject: ent:definition-ref
requirements.canonical: A DefinitionRef or FieldReference in a `with` statement SHALL refer to a definition or field, respectively, which is within the module, group or definition to which the `with` statement is associated.
requirements.original: a) _DefinitionRef and FieldReference shall refer to a definition or field respectively which is within the module,_ group or definition to which the with statement is associated.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.condition: multiple attributes of the same kind are allowed
requirements.canonical: If multiple attributes of the same kind are allowed in a `with` statement, all of them SHALL be without an additional modifier (`override`, `@local`) or all of them SHALL have the same modifier.
requirements.original: b) In case multiple attributes of the same type are allowed, all of them shall be without an additional modifier (override, @local) or the modifier shall be the same for all attributes.

ambiguity.issue: 'type' is used for the kind of attribute (encode, variant, ...), which can be confused with TTCN-3 types.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: Dot notation in the FreeText part of an attribute SHALL NOT be used in attributes other than variant attributes.
requirements.original: c) Dot notation in the FreeText part is allowed for variant attributes only.

requirements.subject: ent:display-attribute
requirements.canonical: A display attribute IS allowing the specification of display attributes related to specific presentation formats.
requirements.original: Display attributes allow the specification of display attributes related to specific presentation formats.

requirements.subject: ent:display-attribute
requirements.canonical: The display attribute IS introduced by the keyword `display`.
requirements.original: display

requirements.subject: ent:language-element
requirements.canonical: Every TTCN-3 language element MAY have display attributes that specify how the language element is displayed, e.g. in a tabular format.
requirements.original: All TTCN-3 language elements can have display attributes to specify how particular language elements shall be displayed in, for example, a tabular format.

requirements.subject: ent:display-attribute
requirements.canonical: Special attribute strings related to the display attributes for the graphical presentation format ARE defined in ETSI ES 201 873-3.
requirements.original: Special attribute strings related to the display attributes for the graphical presentation format can be found in ETSI ES 201 873-3 [i.2].

requirements.subject: ent:display-attribute
requirements.canonical: A user MAY define other display attributes.
requirements.original: Other display attributes may be defined by the user.

requirements.subject: ent:user-defined-attribute
requirements.canonical: Because user-defined attributes are not standardized, the interpretation of a user-defined attribute MAY differ between tools or MAY not be supported.
requirements.original: NOTE: Because user-defined attributes are not standardized, the interpretation of these attributes may differ between tools or even may not be supported.

requirements.subject: ent:display-attribute
requirements.canonical: At most one display attribute SHALL be applied to each definition, each individual field reference or each language element to which a `with` statement is associated.
requirements.original: a) At most one display attribute shall be applied to each definition, each individual field reference or language element to which a with statement is associated.

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: General or particular encoding rules MAY be specified by using encode and variant attributes.
requirements.original: In TTCN-3, general or particular encoding rules can be specified by using encode and variant attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: An encode attribute IS allowing references to specific encoding rules.
requirements.original: Encoding attributes allow references to specific encoding rules.

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: The encode attribute IS introduced by the keyword `encode`.
requirements.original: encode

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-rule
requirements.canonical: An encoding rule IS defining how a value, template, etc. is encoded and transmitted over a communication port and how received signals are decoded.
requirements.original: Encoding rules define how a particular value, template, etc. shall be encoded and transmitted over a communication port and how received signals shall be decoded.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-language
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language IS NOT having a default encoding mechanism.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 does not have a default encoding mechanism.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-rule
requirements.canonical: Encoding rules and encoding directives ARE defined in some manner external to TTCN-3.
requirements.original: This means that encoding rules or encoding directives are defined in some external manner to TTCN-3.

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: The encode attribute IS associating a referenced encoding rule or encoding directive with a TTCN-3 definition.
requirements.original: The encode attribute allows the association of some referenced encoding rule or encoding directive to be made to a TTCN-3 definition.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-rule
requirements.canonical: The manner in which the actual encoding rules are defined (e.g. prose, functions) IS outside the scope of the core language standard.
requirements.original: The manner in which the actual encoding rules are defined (e.g. prose, functions, etc.) is outside the scope of the present document.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: no specific encoding rules are referenced
requirements.canonical: If no specific encoding rules are referenced, the encoding SHALL be a matter for the individual implementation.
requirements.original: If no specific rules are referenced then encoding shall be a matter for individual implementation.

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: Encoding attributes ARE in most cases used in a hierarchical manner.
requirements.original: In most cases encoding attributes will be used in a hierarchical manner.

requirements.subject: ent:encoding-hierarchy
requirements.canonical: In the encoding hierarchy the top level IS the entire module, the next level IS a group and the lowest level IS an individual type or definition.
requirements.original: The top-level is the entire module, the next level is a group and the lowest is an individual type or definition:

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: An encode attribute associated with a module IS applying to all types defined in the module, including the built-in TTCN-3 types.
requirements.original: a) module: encoding applies to all types defined in the module, including TTCN-3 types (built-in types);

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear how a module-level encode attribute can apply to built-in types, which are not defined in the module; read as: built-in types used in the module are encoded with the module rule.
readings: An encode attribute associated with a module IS applying to all types defined in the module and to built-in types used within the module.
An encode attribute associated with a module IS applying only to types defined in the module, and built-in types are included only where they are referenced by such definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: An encode attribute associated with a group IS applying to the user-defined type definitions of the group.
requirements.original: b) group: encoding applies to a group of user-defined type definitions;

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: An encode attribute associated with a type or definition IS applying to that single user-defined type or definition.
requirements.original: c) type or definition: encoding applies to a single user-defined type or definition;

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.canonical: An encode attribute associated with a field IS applying to that field of a record type, set type or template.
requirements.original: d) field: encoding applies to a field in a record or set type or template.

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement MAY contain more than one encode attribute.
requirements.original: The with statement may contain more than one encode attribute.

requirements.subject: ent:encode-attribute
requirements.condition: the with statement contains more than one encode attribute
requirements.canonical: If a `with` statement contains more than one encode attribute, multiple encodings ARE supported in the context where the attribute is used.
requirements.original: In this case, multiple encodings are supported in the context where the attribute is used.

requirements.subject: ent:setencode-operation
requirements.canonical: The encoding used in encoding and decoding operations MAY be selected dynamically by the `setencode` operation, by a parameter of the predefined codec functions, or inside the codec implementation.
requirements.original: The encoding used in the encoding and decoding operations can be selected dynamically by using the setencode operation (clause C.5), as a parameter of predefined codec functions (clause C.5) or inside the codec implementation.

non_requirement.reason: introduction of the restrictions list; extracted from items 27.2-s011..s013
introduction of the restrictions list; extracted from item 27.3-s008
states that clause 27.4 has no restrictions in addition to the general static rules of clause 5
